full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali J : This Rule is directed against the Judgment and Order dated 20-12-94 passed by the First Labour Court, Dhaka Respondent No. 1 in complaint Case No. 29 of 1992 (Annexure-D to the petition). The facts leading to this writ petition are that the respondent No. 2 who was a retired army person was verbally appointed on 1-2-91 as Chief Inspector under the company named Shield Limited, and subsequently the respondent No. 2 was, by a letter dated 14-7-91 allowed to enjoy financial allowance of Taka 200.00 in addition to his salary of Taka 2000.00. The main business of the company is to supply the security guards to local and foreign establishments and also to different foreign embassies and the respondent No. 2 was engaged to collect demands from different establishment and supply security guards to different establishments. He was not in any way connected with the management of the company. While the respondent No. 2 had been discharging his duties as such a conspiracy was started against him to oust him from the Dhaka office of the company and pursuant to that the first party was verbally directed to join Northern Beverage Industry in North Bengal. The respondent No. 2 informed the petitioner/employer about the difficulties faced by him for not giving the order in writing, and thereafter the petitioner-second-party terminated the service of the respondent No. 2 by termination letter dated 8-4-92 without giving any valid reason, and he was not given termination benefit. The respondent No. 2, against this termination letter, submitted grievance petition on 20-4-92 by registered post which was not duly delivered to the second party and it was returned to the respondent No. 2 with the remark as refused and thereafter the respondent No. 2 filed a complaint petition under section 25 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act 1965, before the First Labour Court Dhaka praying for reinstatement or alternatively for awarding termination benefit. 

 2. The second party, writ petitioner being the General Manager of the company contested the case by filing written statements denying material allegations as made in the petition of complaint and contended that the respondent No. 2 was appointed under second party as Chief Inspector and due to structural change of the establishment the first party ie respondent No. 2 was transferred to another establishment under the company but the respondent No. 2 refused to join there and ultimately the employer second party terminated his service. The petitioner second party further asserted in their written statements that the case is not maintainable as the first party was not a worker and no grievance notice was duly served upon the second party. 

 4. The respondent Nb. 2 filed an affidavit-in-opposition wherein he has stated that he was discharging duties under the employer-petitioner as worker and he was not employed in a managerial or administrative capacity although his appointment was made as Chief Inspector. 

 (i) in a factory, any person working as manager of the factory, 

 (ii) in any shop, commercial establishment or industrial establishment, carried on by or on behalf of a local authority, the officer appointed, the chief executive officer of that authority, and 

 (iii) in relation to any other shop, commercial establishment or industrial establishment, every Director, Manager, Secretary, Agent or other officer or person concerned with management thereof and responsible to the owner for the supervision and control of such shop, commercial establishment or industrial establishment." 

 6. From the foregoing definition it is crystal clear that MR Chowdhury, being the General Manager, Shield Limited, is the employer of the first party. It is not the case of the petitioner that the General Manager Shield Limited the petitioner before us was not under the employment of the said company when the termination letter was issued and when the grievance petition was submitted. On the other hand, we find from the papers submitted before the Labour Court that the termination order dated 8-4-92 was issued by Mr. MR Chowdhury being the General Manager of the company. The grievance notice was also addressed to him and Mr. MR Chowdhury, in the capacity of Manager of the company contested the case before the Labour Court by filing written statement and the same General Manager has also filed this instant writ petition. So, the petitioner cannot now say that he is not the employer of the first party, respondent No. 2. 

 7. Mr. MA Wahhab Miah next submitted, although half-heartedly, that the respondent No. 2 is not a worker and as such he cannot come before the Labour Court to seek relief under section 25 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. We find from the written statements filed by the petitioner before the Labour Court that a plea was taken that the first party was an Officer and he was discharging his duties in a managerial, administrative and supervisory capacity. It does appear from the Judgment of the Labour Court that this point was not at all agitated before the Labour Court, nor the petitioner placed any materials before the Labour Court showing that first party was not a worker, nor the petitioner adduced any oral evidence to establish their case in this respect. 

 8. Mr. Md. Habibur Rahman Miah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2 submitted that the petitioner could not place any materials before the Labour Court to prove that the first party is not a worker or that the first party was discharging duties in a managerial or administrative capacity. 

 "A person does not cease to be a ''worker'' merely because he is employed in a supervisory capacity. To be able to say that he is not a worker it has to be established further that he exercises functions mainly of a managerial or administrative nature. 

 "The term "worker" as is defined in section 2(V) of the Act does contemplate not only a person to be employed in the work for productive purposes in any commercial or industrial establishment, but also embraces a person who on being employed does any skilled, unskilled, manual, technical, trade promotional or clerical work for hire or reward, whether the term of employment be express or implied. But a person does not came within the category of "worker" who is employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, or who, being employed in a supervisory capacity, exercises, either by nature of the duties attached to the office or by reason of power vested in him, functions mainly of managerial or administrative nature."
